cards.title: Choose the Professional Seller Plan for Volume Sellers
cards.summary: Pick Amazon's Professional plan if you'll sell more than ~40 units per month; otherwise the free Individual plan may fit.
cards.use_when: Account setup and pricing: deciding which Amazon seller plan fits your expected order volume.

cards.title: Avoid Account-Denial Traps When Applying as a Seller
cards.summary: Prevent application bans by using clean, consistent information, a credit card and a business email.
cards.use_when: Account setup: submitting an Amazon seller application and you want to avoid denials or permanent bans.

cards.title: Prepare Documents and Details Before Applying
cards.summary: Assemble clean ID, bank, and business documents before starting your Amazon seller application to avoid rejection.
cards.use_when: Account setup: you are about to sign up for Amazon Seller Central and want the application to go smoothly.

cards.title: Set Up Your Business Identity Before Listing
cards.summary: Register a business entity that matches your Amazon account to keep finances separate and reduce liability.
cards.use_when: Account setup and brand-building: choosing the legal structure behind your Amazon store.

cards.title: Prepare product identifiers and check Brand Registry eligibility
cards.summary: Set up identifiers and brand documentation for an own-brand Amazon listing without assuming ranking or protection guarantees.
cards.use_when: Brand-building and product-page setup: you're selling a private-label or own-brand product and want listing control and enhanced content.

cards.title: Apply Conversion Psychology to Packaging and Listings
cards.summary: Treat branding and listing content as premium presentation tools that justify higher prices and improve conversion.
cards.use_when: Product-page and merchandising decisions: writing your title, bullets, images and designing packaging to convert more visitors.

cards.title: Coordinate genuine launch demand with listing readiness and stock
cards.summary: Align an opted-in audience, truthful launch communications and inventory to support an Amazon launch.
cards.use_when: Launch strategy: you have an FBA product ready and want to rank on Amazon search quickly.

cards.title: Use Crowdfunding to Fund Your First Production Run
cards.summary: Raise product cost and shipping through pre-orders before spending your own money on manufacturing.
cards.use_when: Replenishment and cash management: you need capital for a first production run or a new product before you have Amazon revenue.

cards.title: Check Manufacturer MOQs and Shipping Before Committing
cards.summary: Send a short inquiry to multiple manufacturers and compare MOQ, price and shipping to pick the fit before ordering.
cards.use_when: Sourcing: choosing a manufacturer for a private-label or own-product FBA launch.

cards.title: Budget for Q4 Inventory and Avoid Stockouts
cards.summary: Plan Q4 inventory early because holiday demand is roughly triple, and stockouts collapse ranking and revenue.
cards.use_when: Replenishment and fulfillment: planning order timing around peak selling season.

cards.title: Judge FBA Viability on the Fee Structure
cards.summary: Compare FBA's per-order pick-and-pack cost against self-shipping to decide fulfillment mode and price your product.
cards.use_when: Fulfillment decision and unit economics: choosing FBA vs merchant-fulfilled and setting a price that covers total costs.

cards.title: Use Brand Registry to Protect Your Listing From Edits
cards.summary: Use eligible brand tools to manage listing accuracy and report infringement, while continuing to monitor catalog changes.
cards.use_when: Retention and listing protection: your own-brand product is live and you want to prevent tampering and unlock richer PDP content.

cards.title: Match Amazon Setup Choices to Your Business Model
cards.summary: Choose account, plan and branding options based on whether you resell others' products or sell your own brand.
cards.use_when: Account setup and product selection: deciding your path (arbitrage/wholesale/resale vs. private label/own-brand) before applying.

cards.title: Write Clean, Professional Amazon Support Communications
cards.summary: Treat every message to Amazon like a professional job application to reduce friction on account issues.
cards.use_when: Account management: disputing a suspension, asking for an account change, or clarifying a verification issue with Amazon seller support.

cards.title: Retail arbitrage prep: seller account + scanning app
cards.summary: Set up an Amazon seller account and the Amazon Seller app before sourcing so you can scan barcodes in-store and see live price, fees and gating.
cards.use_when: Product selection for a new or cash-constrained store: you want fast-turn inventory to flip on Amazon with minimal upfront capital.

cards.title: Evaluate Featured Offer competitiveness without automatic undercutting
cards.summary: Assess price, availability, delivery and seller performance together when competing on a shared ASIN.
cards.use_when: Managing pricing and fulfillment for a legitimate reseller offer on an existing Amazon ASIN.

cards.title: Finding arbitrage deals in-store and online
cards.summary: Source clearance and discounted multi-packs where the Amazon 90-day median price is roughly double your buy cost after fees, favouring light non-bulky ungated items.
cards.use_when: Sourcing products for an Amazon reseller operation, whether walking a store or scanning deal pages from your desk.

cards.title: Pricing and prep when listing arbitrage inventory
cards.summary: List scanned inventory as FBA, match barcodes, declare battery/dangerous-goods details, and set prices with min/max so automated repricing protects the Buy Box.
cards.use_when: Listing arbitrage stock and managing prices on Amazon once units are in your hands or sent to FBA.

cards.title: Managing seller feedback and product-review mix-ups
cards.summary: Separate seller feedback from product reviews and resolve order problems without linking remedies to ratings.
cards.use_when: Running ongoing account health on an FBA or arbitrage store where seller feedback affects Buy Box eligibility and order volume.

cards.title: Restocking signals for arbitrage inventory
cards.summary: Amazon indicates restock timing and fast-selling SKUs tell you when to reorder from a store or website while the deal is still live.
cards.use_when: Replenishment decisions for limited-time or seasonal arbitrage products so you do not sit on stock or miss sellable windows.

cards.title: Private-label start-up cost breakdown
cards.summary: A worked private-label launch cost roughly $2,150 before sales: research tool, design, barcodes, seller account, samples, manufacturing and freight.
cards.use_when: Pricing out a first private-label product launch and deciding how much cash the business needs before the first sale.

cards.title: Month-by-month P&L and the referral/FBA/PPC fee structure
cards.summary: Every dollar of revenue is reduced by a roughly 15% referral fee, FBA pick-pack-ship fees and PPC spend, so read revenue as gross and track net profit per month.
cards.use_when: Financial planning and pricing decisions on an Amazon store, and judging whether a listing is genuinely profitable after fees and ads.

cards.title: Use Amazon keywords as demand research
cards.summary: Treat Amazon as a search engine: find keywords with meaningful search volume and low competition to pick a product people are already searching to buy.
cards.use_when: Product selection for private label or a new category, before committing inventory spend.

cards.title: Launch one SKU, not four colours
cards.summary: Splitting a first order across colour variants multiplies listings, packaging and inventory risk; launch a single SKU with all effort behind it.
cards.use_when: Deciding variant strategy and initial order composition for a private-label launch or first bundle line.

cards.title: Plan for success: avoid stockouts
cards.summary: Running out of inventory during a ramp loses ranking and bestseller status; hold excess or reorder early enough to survive a good launch and seasonal peaks.
cards.use_when: Order sizing and replenishment planning around launch and peak seasons such as Christmas.

cards.title: Sell a differentiated passion product, not generic private label
cards.summary: Generic private-label items blend in and stall even with good PPC; a differentiated product can sustain momentum and extend to your own site and other channels.
cards.use_when: Choosing what to build a brand around, and deciding whether to keep pushing a me-too product or pivot.

cards.title: Launch quickly once the product is ready
cards.summary: Delaying a finished product ties up cash and loses the recurring monthly profit it could have produced; get to launch in months, not years.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to shortcut research paralysis, outsource help, or take a course when a finished product is sitting unlaunched.

cards.title: Avoid the three launch mistakes that killed $17.5K+
cards.summary: A seller's post-mortem on over-SKU'ing, stockouts and private labeling, with the corrective playbook for each.
cards.use_when: Planning a first (or next) Amazon launch and deciding how many variations to order, how deep to stock, and whether to private-label an existing product.

cards.title: Price band and margin math for Amazon products
cards.summary: Pick products between ~$15 and ~$85 with the $25–$30 sweet spot, and check per-unit profit after Amazon's take.
cards.use_when: Screening a product candidate for pricing viability before committing to sourcing or a listing.

cards.title: Rule out bad product categories before hunting ideas
cards.summary: A pre-screen checklist that eliminates products with structural problems before you waste research time.
cards.use_when: Filtering candidate products so you don't invest in categories that fail on shipping, seasonality, competition or identity.

cards.title: Confirm demand is real with Best Sellers and New Releases
cards.summary: Use Amazon's own best seller and new release lists to see what's selling now, then estimate revenue per product.
cards.use_when: Validating that a category or niche still supports new entrants, or sizing how much a specific listing is doing.

cards.title: Magnet keyword mining with title density to find unserved products
cards.summary: Start from a topic you know, mine Amazon search terms, and filter for keywords with real volume but few competing listings.
cards.use_when: Generating product ideas in a niche where you have knowledge or interest, especially to find a product that doesn't yet exist.

cards.title: Cerebro reverse-lookup: keywords that actually convert for a competitor
cards.summary: Pull the search terms driving sales for a specific listing to find adjacent unmet demand.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a niche you already identified, or looking for a variant product idea adjacent to a proven listing.

cards.title: Amazon autocomplete + Google Trends/Keyword Planner to spot underserved variants
cards.summary: A free research loop: harvest Amazon autocomplete suggestions, then check trend direction and cross-market demand.
cards.use_when: Looking for free product-idea signals and testing whether a keyword has growing demand in both Google and Amazon.

cards.title: Blackbox filtering to surface high-sales, low-review opportunities
cards.summary: Reverse-search Amazon for listings meeting your price, revenue, review and category criteria — then mine their complaints.
cards.use_when: Screening a broad set of candidate products against your target price, revenue and competition quality in minutes.

cards.title: Four product archetypes to build your listing around
cards.summary: Premium, first-mover, evergreen and passion product — positioning choices that shape price, ad spend and longevity.
cards.use_when: Deciding how to position a product (and how to write PDP copy and price it) once a candidate niche is chosen.

cards.title: Idea Generator: turn your own daily friction into product specs
cards.summary: Systematically inventory what you touch and do, then ask improvement questions to generate real product ideas and differentiators.
cards.use_when: When you need product ideas, or when you need a differentiation angle and PDP story for a product you already sell.

cards.title: Mine trend reports to find rising demand to build products against
cards.summary: Frameworks from a 2023 trend report for translating macro consumer shifts into Amazon product angles.
cards.use_when: Scanning for emerging niches, or repositioning an existing product line to match a rising consumer value.

cards.title: How much can you actually make on Amazon: a quick reality check
cards.summary: A repeatable method to size a category's earnings without assuming you'll replicate top sellers.
cards.use_when: Setting revenue expectations for a new Amazon product or evaluating whether a niche's ceiling justifies the effort.

cards.title: Turn Personal Interests Into Amazon Product Ideas
cards.summary: Mine your own interests, hobbies and daily frustrations, then validate them as Amazon search demand instead of guessing at random products.
cards.use_when: You're starting product selection for an Amazon FBA store and have no candidate products yet.

cards.title: Systematically Narrow Amazon's Category Tree to a Niche
cards.summary: Use Amazon's Best Sellers category tree with an interest rating to cut 20,000+ subcategories down to a shortlist worth researching.
cards.use_when: You're doing broad product selection and want a repeatable way to screen Amazon categories instead of browsing aimlessly.

cards.title: Mine Credit Card, Amazon Browse and Google History for Product Ideas
cards.summary: Your own spending and search history reveal categories where you'd be a credible, motivated seller.
cards.use_when: Product selection is stalled and you can't name a product you'd be excited to build.

cards.title: Why Cheap Products Fail and the $15–$85 Price Band
cards.summary: The source's core price filter: cheap, low-barrier products invite price wars and PPC losses, while the $15–$85 band supports impulse purchase and margin.
cards.use_when: You're choosing a selling price or screening a product candidate on price before ordering inventory.

cards.title: Screen Out Trend, Seasonal and Restricted Products
cards.summary: Avoid product categories whose demand window or compliance burden makes inventory risky for a new FBA seller.
cards.use_when: You're shortlisting products and need to disqualify unsuitable categories before ordering.

cards.title: Find Product Gaps by Reading Competitor Reviews and Size Ranges
cards.summary: Use the 'hole in the market' method: identify a missing size, variant or fix from competitor reviews and existing listings.
cards.use_when: You're choosing a product to improve rather than invent, and want a defensible point of difference.

cards.title: Verify a Niche Isn't Brand-Dominated Before Entering
cards.summary: Check whether a dominant brand already owns the category before you try to compete there.
cards.use_when: You're evaluating a product category and deciding whether a new seller can realistically win listings.

cards.title: Pack Titles With the Exact Phrases Buyers Search
cards.summary: Amazon is a purchase-intent search engine; naming and titling your product with real search phrases puts you in front of buyers who want that exact thing.
cards.use_when: You're writing your product title and back-end keywords, or deciding whether a product idea has enough keyword surface to work.

cards.title: Confirm Demand and Value Before You Commit Inventory
cards.summary: Two baseline checks the source says new sellers skip: there must be real demand, and the product must solve a problem worth paying for.
cards.use_when: You're about to commit to a product and need a go/no-go check before sampling and manufacturing.

cards.title: Model Amazon Fees, Landed Cost and Budget Before Choosing
cards.summary: Know your numbers early — manufacturing, freight, Amazon fees and your cash runway — because the product choice is constrained by the math.
cards.use_when: You're deciding between product candidates and need to know what each one will cost you to launch.

cards.title: Make a Free Physical Prototype From a Manufacturer's Sample
cards.summary: Get to a physical mockup cheaply by mocking up with stationery first, then requesting a free blank sample from a manufacturer.
cards.use_when: You've picked a product and need to see and feel it before paying for tooling or design.

cards.title: Crowdfund Your Launch Instead of Self-Funding Inventory
cards.summary: Use pre-orders on a crowdfunding platform plus social content to fund design, manufacturing and freight.
cards.use_when: You have a validated product and prototype but limited cash for design, tooling and inventory.

cards.title: Choose Air vs Sea Freight for First Inventory
cards.summary: Trade freight cost against speed when shipping first inventory from overseas, especially against pre-order promises.
cards.use_when: You're arranging inbound shipment for your first or reorder inventory and deciding air vs sea.

cards.title: Use a Premium Brand and Packaging to Justify a Higher Price
cards.summary: Branding lets two identically-priced-to-make products sell at very different prices, changing profit per sale.
cards.use_when: You're setting your listing price and designing packaging, logo and brand identity for a new product.

cards.title: Hire Low-Cost Design and Support Help From OnlineJobs.ph
cards.summary: Staff ongoing design, editing, social and customer-service work with full-time overseas hires at low hourly rates.
cards.use_when: You're running an Amazon brand and need recurring creative or support labor without agency costs.

cards.title: Pre-orders and crowdfunding to fund first manufacturing run
cards.summary: Using a crowdfunding or pre-order campaign to collect cash before paying manufacturing and freight de-risks a first inventory buy.
cards.use_when: You are launching a first product and don't have cash for manufacturing plus freight, and deciding whether to build a pre-order/crowdfunding page before committing to a production run.

cards.title: Customer email list as an Amazon launch accelerator
cards.summary: Building an email list during stockouts lets you concentrate sales and reviews into the first days of an Amazon listing, which the source says improves search ranking.
cards.use_when: You are out of stock, pre-launch, or relaunching an Amazon listing and want to spike early sales velocity to push search rank.

cards.title: Air vs sea freight decision for replenishment
cards.summary: Sea freight costs far less per kilogram but takes weeks; air freight is only justified when being in stock is worth more than the freight premium.
cards.use_when: You are replenishing Amazon inventory and deciding whether to pay for air freight, especially ahead of a peak season or when you are already out of stock.

cards.title: Amazon FBA unit economics breakdown for a first product
cards.summary: A worked month-by-month P&L showing that Amazon revenue is reduced by product cost, a 15% referral fee, per-unit pick-and-pack fees, and miscellaneous fees.
cards.use_when: You are pricing a private-label or passion product and need a line-item model of what actually comes out of Amazon revenue.

cards.title: Judging the 15% Amazon referral fee against paid traffic
cards.summary: The source treats Amazon's 15% referral fee as a substitute for marketing spend, worth paying because the platform supplies buyer traffic.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to sell primarily on Amazon versus your own site, or setting prices that must absorb Amazon's fee.

cards.title: Selling out during a viral spike: redirect demand instead of pausing
cards.summary: When a viral post drains your stock, keep selling through a backup channel rather than letting the demand evaporate.
cards.use_when: Your Amazon inventory hits zero while a social post, press hit, or ad is still driving traffic to the product.

cards.title: Building a brand on social media to create compounding product demand
cards.summary: Consistent content around a topic you actually know produces demand spikes and press opportunities that a listing alone won't generate.
cards.use_when: You are planning demand generation for a specialty product and deciding where to invest content effort alongside Amazon SEO.

cards.title: Passion-product positioning versus wholesale, arbitrage and private label
cards.summary: The source argues a unique product you are personally invested in outperforms commodity sourcing models and opens extra channels.
cards.use_when: You are choosing which Amazon selling model to pursue, or deciding whether your product is differentiated enough to price above commodity alternatives.

cards.title: Diagnosing seasonal demand swings before abandoning a product
cards.summary: A twelve-month view shows predictable slumps and holiday peaks, so judge a product on the year rather than a three-month decline.
cards.use_when: Your Amazon sales are falling for several consecutive months and you are deciding whether to cut the product, hold inventory, or expand channels.

cards.title: Diversifying into wholesale when slow Amazon sales leave you overstocked
cards.summary: Sitting on excess inventory is a reason to open wholesale, Etsy and international channels rather than discounting on Amazon.
cards.use_when: You have excess Amazon inventory and stagnant sales and want to move units through other channels.

cards.title: Freight and freight-driven landed cost as the lever on margin
cards.summary: Switching freight mode can improve margin even when revenue falls, because landed cost per unit drops.
cards.use_when: Your Amazon revenue is trending down and you need to protect profit without raising price or cutting ads.

cards.title: Analysis paralysis: launch timing matters more than a perfect supplier choice
cards.summary: Delaying a launch to perfect a decision costs more than the mistake you are avoiding, per the presenter's retrospective.
cards.use_when: You are stuck comparing suppliers, product ideas or listing details and delaying your first Amazon order.

cards.title: Outsourcing the non-revenue tasks in an Amazon business
cards.summary: Delegate packing, editing and customer service so your time goes to the activities that actually drive sales.
cards.use_when: You are handling fulfillment, customer messages or video editing yourself and your marketing or sourcing work is slipping.

cards.title: Under-ordering inventory as the most expensive recurring mistake
cards.summary: Chronic under-ordering because of fear caps growth more than most other errors, per the source's own retrospective.
cards.use_when: You are deciding order quantity for your next Amazon production run while demand is trending up or a viral moment is in progress.

cards.title: Finding suppliers on Alibaba with trade assurance and verified filtering
cards.summary: Filter Alibaba to trade-assured, verified suppliers and review their operating history before contacting them.
cards.use_when: You are sourcing a product from overseas suppliers for your Amazon listing and need to screen manufacturers before paying anyone.

cards.title: Sourcing US-based manufacturers via Thomasnet, Google and phone calls
cards.summary: For products that need domestic manufacturing, use US directories and call rather than email to build a stronger connection.
cards.use_when: You need a domestic manufacturer for your product, for example when regulatory, safety or quality-control concerns make overseas production unattractive.

cards.title: Cold outreach at scale to find a manufacturer for a novel product
cards.summary: Blasting a clear, specific email to dozens of manufacturers across ten pages of search results is a workable way to find one willing to make an unusual product.
cards.use_when: You are sourcing a manufacturer for an unconventional product and most suppliers have said no or not replied.

cards.title: Questions to ask a manufacturer before committing
cards.summary: A short list of questions covering minimum order quantity, full cost structure, timeline and scope of work prevents surprises after you commit.
cards.use_when: You have found a manufacturer willing to produce your product and are preparing to place a first order.

cards.title: Always ordering a physical sample before a production run
cards.summary: A paid sample validates product quality and taste before committing thousands to a production run.
cards.use_when: You have found a manufacturer and are about to place your first bulk order.

cards.title: Learning from refusals: phone calls as supplier education
cards.summary: Rejection calls are where manufacturers reveal why a product is hard to make and how it might be done, making you a more credible buyer next time.
cards.use_when: You are sourcing an unusual product and manufacturers keep declining; you want to convert those calls into useful technical intelligence.

cards.title: Finding competitors' manufacturers through Jungle Scout supplier lookups
cards.summary: Jungle Scout's supplier database can reveal the manufacturers behind existing Amazon products by company name or ASIN.
cards.use_when: You want a shortlist of vetted manufacturers already producing products similar to the one you plan to sell.

cards.title: Using industry trade shows to build a manufacturer list
cards.summary: Trade show exhibitor lists for your product category are a ready-made roster of suppliers and manufacturers.
cards.use_when: You need a broad, category-specific supplier list and directories aren't producing enough candidates.

cards.title: Sourcing European manufacturers for a non-US seller
cards.summary: Directory sites such as Europages help sellers based outside the US find manufacturers in their own region.
cards.use_when: Your business is based in the UK or Europe and you want a local manufacturer for lead times, communication or regulatory reasons.

cards.title: Assuming one manufacturer won't do everything
cards.summary: Specialist manufacturers often handle only their core step, so plan for a second supplier for packaging or finishing.
cards.use_when: You are mapping your production process and budgeting for how many suppliers and handoffs you need.

cards.title: Find manufacturers via reverse ASIN lookup and industry conventions
cards.summary: Three alternative sourcing channels for identifying real manufacturers rather than resellers: reverse ASIN tools, trade-show exhibitor lists, and regional directories.
cards.use_when: Product selection and sourcing: you have a validated product idea and need to find factories capable of making it, but don't know where to start.

cards.title: Order 3-6 months of inventory as your first production run
cards.summary: First-run order sizing balances risk of dead stock against stockouts, with 3-6 months of projected sales as the source's recommended default.
cards.use_when: Replenishment and first production run planning: deciding how many units to commit to before you have real sales data.
